clue.text: Sound unit former Russian soldier sent back to claim Sark etc

indicators.note: to claim means the reversed soldier's name takes the islands into its middle
sent back means the soldier's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Alexander Lebed was a Russian general and politician
Sark is one of the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI

explanation.surface: An old Russian soldier is packed off home to stake a claim on a Channel island.
explanation.walkthrough: Lebed was a general in the Soviet army; 'sent back' reverses his name and 'to claim' wraps it round the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A decibel is the standard measure of loudness, a unit for sound.

clue.text: Stop to request fabric

parts.note: to dam a river is to stop its flow
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A halt to ask for some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven fabric, often linen or silk.

clue.text: Coptic leader and god in agreement

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Coptic

parts.note: Horus is the falcon-headed god of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: An Egyptian church head and a deity see eye to eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Coptic Christianity is Egyptian, as is the god.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorus of approval is a widespread agreement voiced together.

clue.text: Union supporter depends on mother to break proposal

indicators.note: to break means the proposal is split open to take the other pieces

parts.note: a bid is an offer or proposal
rides on means depends on, as in everything rides on this
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A trade union backer relies on mother to wreck a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union supporter' suggests trade unions, but the union is a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is a union, and the bride's attendant supports her at it.

clue.text: Customer initially going in to draw money

indicators.note: going in means the customer's first letter is put inside

parts.note: to lure is to draw or entice

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of Customer

explanation.surface: A shopper first goes in to withdraw cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, especially gained dishonourably, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: As to that extent, very deep then?

parts.note: something very deep is ..., read as three words

explanation.surface: A query about how far something extends, wondering if it is very deep.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction means to the degree that, as in 'insofar as I know'.

clue.text: Beefy stews obtain meat

indicators.note: stews suggests cooking things into a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ham is a meat

explanation.surface: Hearty stews get their meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Botham, the English cricketer, is nicknamed Beefy.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of the former England cricket all-rounder Ian Botham.

clue.text: Green finally absorbed by blue to become greyish-yellow

indicators.note: absorbed by means the final letter goes inside the word for blue

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of Green

explanation.surface: Green is finally taken up by blue to become a muddy colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand as a colour is a pale yellowish-brown or grey shade.

clue.text: Classmate, according to protocol

parts.note: a classmate, split up: form is a school class and an ally is a mate

explanation.surface: A fellow pupil, playing by the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Form is the British school word for a class.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things officially and with ceremony means following protocol.

clue.text: Catholic Asians among rampant extremists

indicators.note: among means the Asians sit between the two outer letters
extremists means the extreme letters of rampant

parts.note: Omanis are people from Oman, in Asia

explanation.surface: Catholic Asians are found among raging fanatics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' looks like people; it means the extreme letters R and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romanist is a sometimes hostile term for a Roman Catholic.

clue.text: I ramble when flipping over tongue

indicators.note: flipping over asks for the words I and ramble to be read backwards

parts.note: to ramble is to roam

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they wander off topic whenever they turn things round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when flipping over' turns I ROAM into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue here means a language; Maori is the language of New Zealand's indigenous people.

clue.text: Sister feeds fish odd question

indicators.note: feeds means the sister is put into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: a cod is a fish
a nun is a religious sister
rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A nun feeding a fish poses a strange question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd question' looks like the definition, but 'odd' belongs to the wordplay, an old sense of strange, and 'feeds' sets the sister inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle or puzzling problem is a kind of question.

clue.text: Lover has to fight for music-maker

parts.note: a squeeze is informal for a boyfriend or girlfriend
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A partner must do battle for an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeezebox is an informal name for an accordion or concertina, an instrument.

clue.text: Story that's spun out?

definitions.meaning: a tale, especially a long rambling one

explanation.surface: A tale that goes on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a tall tale told, and spun thread for knitting.

clue.text: Male agent head-over-heels in love for the current time

indicators.note: in means the reversed pieces go inside the word for love

parts.note: amour is love, from French

indicators.note: head-over-heels means the male and agent are turned upside down

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent

explanation.surface: A man's agent falls madly in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head-over-heels in love' reads as an idiom, but it turns HEREP to PEREH, which goes into AMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit is current multiplied by time, one amp flowing for sixty minutes.

clue.text: Disorganised son blames him for a total mess

indicators.note: disorganised tells us the letters of son, blames and him are in disorder

explanation.surface: A muddled boy points the finger at another for some fiasco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorganised' rearranges SON BLAMES HIM, twelve letters, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A modern coinage for a situation mishandled in every possible way, a complete shambles.

clue.text: Back of Robin Reliant damaged, rear of Subaru caught, parked up?

indicators.note: caught means the last letter of Subaru is held inside the rearranged letters
damaged suggests the car is smashed up, so its letters are rearranged
back of means the last letter of Robin
rear of means the last letter of Subaru

explanation.surface: A Robin Reliant, damaged at the back, has caught a Subaru's rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: A Robin Reliant is a British three-wheeled car. 'damaged' rearranges N plus RELIANT, and 'caught' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A car out of gear sits with the gearbox disengaged, idle as if parked.

clue.text: Planet invaded by second alien simian

indicators.note: invaded by means the planet's name is broken into by the second

parts.note: Mars is a planet
a mo is a moment or second
ET is the alien of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A planet is invaded by a second alien, an ape-like one.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American monkey, a simian.

clue.text: Mate welcoming cryptic Paul into bird's home

indicators.note: welcoming means the bird's home takes the jumbled name inside

parts.note: a cote is a shelter for doves or pigeons

indicators.note: cryptic means the name Paul is made obscure, rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter Paul is welcomed into a dovecote to pair up.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is the setter of this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To mate is to have sex, which is to copulate.

clue.text: Blondie hit song, one's a gas

parts.note: Atomic was a 1980 hit single by the band Blondie
a number is a song in a performance

explanation.surface: A pop song by Blondie is praised as great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's a gas' reads like praise of the song, but it says that the figure 1 belongs to hydrogen, a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen, a gas, has the element number one in the periodic table.

clue.text: Notice depravity in suggestion

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a notice
vice is wickedness or depravity

explanation.surface: A warning about depravity in a hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel offered on what to do is a suggestion.

clue.text: Deposit lolly down underwear?

parts.note: put down a vest is to be ...

explanation.surface: Stashing cash in one's undershirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Lolly is British slang for money; a vest is British for an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting money into something for return is to invest it.

clue.text: Cross cut guarding a paw

indicators.note: guarding means the shortened hybrid surrounds the letter a
cut means the last letter of the hybrid is lopped off

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

explanation.surface: An angry person, cut, protects a paw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims MULE to MUL, and 'guarding' puts A inside: M-A-UL.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle roughly or clumsily, as a bear might, is to paw at something.

clue.text: Potential financial catastrophe endured, not entirely good, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged
not entirely means the last letter of good is dropped

explanation.surface: A likely money crisis was endured, and things were not quite good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims GOOD to GOO; 'unfortunately' scrambles ENDURED plus GOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A coinage blending the euro with Armageddon, for a feared collapse of the single currency.

clue.text: Drive with speed beyond roundabouts?

indicators.note: beyond means the speed comes after the roundabouts

parts.note: two round shapes look like letters O
mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: Driving fast past roundabouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is energy, vigour or drive.

clue.text: Gargantuan gastronome gaily guzzles

indicators.note: guzzles means the words swallow the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A huge gourmet cheerfully gobbles food.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang for enormous or huge.

clue.text: One's hit a racehorse on both sides of shin

indicators.note: both sides of means the first and last letters of shin

parts.note: Red Rum was a famous racehorse, three times winner of the Grand National

explanation.surface: Someone strikes a racehorse on both sides of the shin.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum is a celebrated British steeplechaser; the Grand National is Britain's best-known horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum is struck with sticks, so it is something that gets hit.

clue.text: Tree yielding oil primarily, as it happens

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of oil

parts.note: broadcast live means shown as it happens

explanation.surface: A tree gives oil above all, as it happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is an evergreen tree grown in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Zero in ten has to suffer for one in ten

indicators.note: in means the zero goes inside the word ten

parts.note: taken as written
zero is the figure O
to ail is to suffer or be ill

explanation.surface: A nothing among ten has to endure hardship for one out of ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in ten' looks like a statistic; it is one of the ten nails on the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Each foot has five nails, so one claw-like nail is one of ten on the feet.

clue.text: Government ultimately behind the privileged few — about right, one's gathered

indicators.note: behind means the government's last letter comes after
about means the privileged few surround the letter for right

parts.note: the haves are the well-off, as in haves and have-nots

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of Government

explanation.surface: The government is finally behind the elite, who gather round the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Crops collected at the end of the season are a gathering of produce.
